{{nihongo|'''Susa Shrine'''|須佐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

=== History ===
In ``{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}'', there is a description that Susanoo no Mikoto came to this area after cultivating various areas, did the final cultivation, and said, ``This is a good country, so I will name the land, not Iwaki,'' and named it ``Susa'' to soothe his soul. Since ancient times, it has been considered the main shrine of Susanoo no Mikoto. The Susa clan of {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} is said to have descended from {{ill|Kayanarumi no Kami|Q11294873|qid=Q11294873|lt=Kayana-ryu Mime}}, the son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkuninushi}}.

The former site of the shrine is said to have been on Mt. Miyao to the north of the shrine. The current shrine site is located almost in the center of the basin, and it is thought that it was already in this area during the Middle Ages.

It is described as ``Sosa Shrine'' in ``Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki.'' In the ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', it is listed as ``Susa Shrine'' and is listed as a small shrine. In the medieval period, it was called ``Jusansho Daimyojin'' and ``Omiya Daimyojin,'' and in the early modern period, it was called ``Susa Omiya.''

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), the name was changed to "Susa Shrine" as described in the Engishiki, and in Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was promoted to a local shrine, the following year in the 6th year of Meiji ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in the 33rd year of Meiji ({{ill|1900|Q2034|qid=Q2034}}) to a national shrine.

=== Facilities ===
; Main shrine, Heiden, Worship hall
:: The main shrine is a cultural property designated by Shimane Prefecture and was built in 1861. |publisher=Shimane Prefecture Education Agency Cultural Properties Division}}</ref>. It is a {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|qid=Q387874}} building with a width of 2 rooms (approximately 4 m) and a height of approximately 12 m, and there is a floor (kizahashi) that serves as the entrance to the 1 room on the right. <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.susa-jinja.jp/information/8 |title=Gohonden (designated as an important prefectural cultural property) |access-date=2022-07-13 |publisher=Susa Shrine Official}}</ref>. The one before that is described as 4 rooms in the Omiyako map written in {{ill|Gen'ō|Q1193925|qid=Q1193925}} 2nd year ({{ill|1320|Q5768|qid=Q5768}}).

; Osugi
:: Located behind the main shrine, the tree is estimated to be about 1300 years old, with a trunk circumference of 7 meters and a height of 30 meters. Since {{ill|Hiroyuki Ehara|Q11550701|qid=Q11550701}}'s ``Shinto Travelogue'' was published, many people who were unscrupulous were peeling off the bark of this cedar tree and taking it home with them, so a fence has now been placed around the trunk.

=== Kyougaisha ===
; Itsukushima Shrine
:: Deities enshrined: Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto, Tagoko Hime no Mikoto, Tanatsu Hime no Mikoto ({{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|Q10948069|qid=Q10948069}}). <ref name=":0" /> Also called ``Seidosha'' and ``Haridosha''.
; Suga Shrine
:: Enshrined deity: Suho-no-son. <ref name=":0" /> is also called "Saikagura-san".

=== Festival ===
* January 1st {{ill|Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824}}
* February 3rd {{ill|Setsubun|Q746798|qid=Q746798|lt=Setsubun Festival}}
** {{ill|Kagura|Q1348260|qid=Q1348260}} dedication, {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910|lt=Chino Ring}}, and bean-throwing will be held.
*February 17th Prayer Festival
* April 18th {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}
** Asashi Matsuri - After the regular festival ritual, the festival is carried out from the main shrine to Amaterasu Shrine across the street. |access-date=2022-07-13 |publisher=Susa Shrine Official}}</ref>.
* April 19 Koden Festival
** Ryoou-mai - Performed following the Koden Festival ritual. <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.susa-jinja.jp/event/27/29 |title=Ryoou no Mai |access-date=2022-07-13 |publisher=Susa Shrine Official}}</ref>. It is thought that it was originally danced by a divine being of the Onmyoji type, but was transformed into one.** Hundred-handed Shinji - Archery ritual held in the afternoon to pray for the exorcism of demons and a good harvest.
* June 30th {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910}}
* August 15 Kirimei Shinto ritual
** {{ill|nenbutsu odori|Q11491438|qid=Q11491438}} - Held in the afternoon. Two ritual flowers are erected in the shrine grounds, and beneath them dancers wearing kimono (kimono) form a circle, chanting ``Naamamido'' and dancing monotonously to the beat of the flute. It is a dance with strong {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} color, which is thought to have been influenced by Nembutsu saints in the {{ill|Dengaku|ca|Dengaku|es|Dengaku (música)|fa|دنگاکو|fr|Dengaku|id|Dengaku|it|Dengaku|ja|田楽|ko|덴가쿠 (춤)|pl|Dengaku|ru|Дэнгаку|qid=Q3022455}} style of dance in the medieval period.
* October 17th Autumn Festival
* November 23rd Niinamatsuri
* December 31st Purification
* 15th of every month {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}}

=== Transportation ===
* From {{ill|Izumoshi Station|Q860288|qid=Q860288}}, take the {{ill|Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|qid=Q11352955}} bound for Izumo Susa and get off at Susa bus stop. 3 km walk.
* If you are using a car, there are over 10 parking spaces next to the temple grounds.
